Source: A 16-year-old girl who recently immigrated to the United States from Bolivia presents to her primary care physician with a chief complaint of inattentiveness in school.
On physical exam, you note a young, healthy girl whose neurological exam is within normal limits.
She is not sexually active and does not intend to become pregnant in the near future.
The patient states she is not doing this intentionally.
Nothing has helped the patient change her behavior, including parent-teacher conferences or punishment.
The patient has an unknown medical history and is currently not on any medications.
The patient's teacher describes her as occasionally "daydreaming" for periods of time during where the patient does not respond or participate in school activities.
The only other concern that the patient's mother has is that, upon awakening, she notices that sometimes the patient's arm will jerk back and forth.
Her temperature is 98.6°F (37°C), blood pressure is 112/74 mmHg, pulse is 63/min, and respirations are 11/min.
